claim: The Drosophila lateral horn (LH) is implicated in innate behavior.
source: In Drosophila, one higher olfactory centre, the lateral horn (LH), is implicated in innate behaviour.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about the LH.

claim: A collection of split-GAL4 driver lines providing genetic access to 82 LH cell types was generated.
source: We generate a collection of split-GAL4 driver lines providing genetic access to 82 LH cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Approximately 30% of LH projections converge with outputs from the mushroom body.
source: We find ~30% of LH projections converge with outputs from the mushroom body, site of olfactory learning and memory.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding stated in the abstract and supported by overlap analysis data in the manuscript.

claim: Optogenetic activation of specific LH cell types drives changes in valence behavior.
source: Using optogenetic activation, we identify LH cell types that drive changes in valence behavior or specific locomotor programs.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 9.

claim: Optogenetic activation of specific LH cell types drives specific locomotor programs.
source: Using optogenetic activation, we identify LH cell types that drive changes in valence behavior or specific locomotor programs.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 10.

claim: The olfactory system is only one synapse from the sensory periphery to the central brain.
source: The olfactory system is only one synapse from the sensory periphery to the central brain, with common anatomical and circuit logic across the animal kingdom (Su et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: After the first processing relay, the olfactory system diverges into at least two pathways.
source: After the first processing relay (the insect antennal lobe or mammalian olfactory bulb) the olfactory system diverges into at least two pathways (Marin et al., 2002; Miyamichi et al., 2011; Sosulski et al., 2011a; Wong et al., 2002)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations to support it.

claim: The insect lateral horn and mammalian cortical amygdala are hardwired, chemotopic circuits thought to mediate innate behaviour.
source: A hardwired, chemotopic circuit that is thought to mediate innate behaviour (the insect lateral horn and mammalian cortical amygdala)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the function of these brain regions.

claim: The insect mushroom body and mammalian piriform cortex are decorrelated, unstructured circuits required for memory storage and retrieval.
source: a decorrelated, unstructured circuit that is required for memory storage and retrieval (insect mushroom body or mammalian piriform cortex) (Choi et al., 2011; Dubnau et al., 2001; Gruntman and Turner, 2013; Heimbeck et al., 2001; McGuire et al., 2001; Parnas et al., 2013; Root et al., 2014a; Sacco and Sacchetti, 2010)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations to support it.

claim: In mice, the cortical amygdala is both necessary and sufficient for innate olfactory responses.
source: In mice the cortical amygdala is both necessary and sufficient for innate olfactory responses; however, the neurons that drive avoidance and attraction intermingle (Root et al., 2014a)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Neurons that drive avoidance and attraction intermingle in the mouse cortical amygdala.
source: In mice the cortical amygdala is both necessary and sufficient for innate olfactory responses; however, the neurons that drive avoidance and attraction intermingle (Root et al., 2014a)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Sensory neurons expressing the same receptor converge to the same glomerulus in the antennal lobe.
source: Sensory neurons expressing the same receptor converge to the same glomerulus, an organizational feature shared with the mammalian brain (Masse et al., 2009; Su et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: Uniglomerular PNs (mPN1s) have their dendrites in a single glomerulus and send axons to the mushroom body (MB) and the lateral horn (LH).
source: Uniglomerular PNs (mPN1s) have their dendrites in a single glomerulus and send axons to the two higher olfactory brain regions, the mushroom body (MB) and the lateral horn (LH) (Figure 1A) (Jefferis et al., 2007; Marin et al., 2002; Wong et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The axons of the PNs connect randomly with different subsets of Kenyon cells in the mushroom body.
source: The axons of the PNs connect randomly with different subsets of Kenyon cells, the intrinsic neurons of the MB (Caron et al., 2013; Eichler et al., 2017; Gruntman and Turner, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: PN-to-LH connectivity is stereotyped and the same PNs connect to the same LH neurons across different animals.
source: In contrast, PN-to-LH connectivity is stereotyped and the same PNs connect to the same LH neurons across different animals (Fişek and Wilson, 2014; Frechter et al., 2019; Jeanne et al., 2018; Jefferis et al., 2007; Kohl et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations to support it.

claim: MB neurotransmission is necessary for the formation, consolidation and retrieval of olfactory memories but dispensable for innate olfactory responses.
source: By spatiotemporally silencing Kenyon cells, many studies have demonstrated that MB neurotransmission is necessary for the formation, consolidation and retrieval of olfactory memories but dispensable for innate olfactory responses (Dubnau et al., 2001; Heimbeck et al., 2001; Krashes et al., 2007; McGuire et al., 2001; Parnas et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations to support it.

claim: The LH is implicated in innate olfactory processing.
source: By spatiotemporally silencing Kenyon cells, many studies have demonstrated that MB neurotransmission is necessary for the formation, consolidation and retrieval of olfactory memories but dispensable for innate olfactory responses (Dubnau et al., 2001; Heimbeck et al., 2001; Krashes et al., 2007; McGuire et al., 2001; Parnas et al., 2013), indirectly implicating the LH in innate olfactory processing.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that MB is not required for innate responses, implying the LH must be involved.

claim: There have been no studies to date manipulating single or small constellations of identified cell types of the adult LH during olfactory behaviour.
source: In contrast to the MB, there have been no studies to date manipulating single or small constellations of identified cell types of the adult LH during olfactory behaviour, due to a lack of reagents available to control LH cell types.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature that motivates the current study.

claim: The total number of cell types with substantial LH dendrite is estimated to be >165.
source: the total number of cell types with substantial LH dendrite is estimated to be >165 (Frechter et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as an estimate from a cited study.

claim: A previous neuroanatomical screen of more than 4000 enhancer trap lines identified only six with clear LH expression.
source: A previous neuroanatomical screen of more than 4000 enhancer trap lines identified only six with clear LH expression (Tanaka et al., 2004)
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a cited study.

claim: 2444 split-GAL4 lines were generated and screened.
source: We generated and screened 2444 split-GAL4 lines (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is a primary methodological detail stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Of the 2444 split-GAL4 lines screened, 1095 split-GAL4 combinations containing both visible and sparse expression were selected for immunohistochemistry and confocal imaging.
source: Of these, 1095 split-GAL4 combinations containing both visible and sparse expression were selected for the second selection step, whole mount immunohistochemistry and confocal imaging (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary methodological detail stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 259 'good' and 123 'ideal' split-GAL4 lines were identified from the 1095 split-GAL4 combinations that were stained and imaged.
source: Of these 1095 split-GAL4 combinations that were stained and imaged, we identified 259 'good' and 123 'ideal' split-GAL4 lines.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claim: 123 'good' and 87 'ideal' split-GAL4 lines that specifically labeled one genetically identifiable group of LH neurons each were selected for use in the current study.
source: We selected a subset of these that specifically labeled one genetically identifiable group of LH neurons each and present 123 of these 'good' and 87 'ideal' split-GAL4 lines for use in the current study.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claim: The split-GAL4 lines covered 82 cell types of the LH.
source: In total our split-GAL4 lines covered 82 cell types of the LH (Figures 2–5, see Supplementary file 1 for summary of all cell types and their anatomical details).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 2-5.

claim: 44 LH output neuron (LHON) cell types were identified.
source: We identified 44 LH output neuron (LHON), 8 LH local neuron (LHLN) and 14 non-antennal lobe input neuron (LHIN) cell types (Figures 2–5, see Figure 1H for an example cell type of each polarity category).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 2-5.

claim: 8 LH local neuron (LHLN) cell types were identified.
source: We identified 44 LH output neuron (LHON), 8 LH local neuron (LHLN) and 14 non-antennal lobe input neuron (LHIN) cell types (Figures 2–5, see Figure 1H for an example cell type of each polarity category).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 2-5.

claim: 14 non-antennal lobe input neuron (LHIN) cell types were identified.
source: We identified 44 LH output neuron (LHON), 8 LH local neuron (LHLN) and 14 non-antennal lobe input neuron (LHIN) cell types (Figures 2–5, see Figure 1H for an example cell type of each polarity category).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 2-5.

claim: Of the identified LHON cell types, 26 were acetylcholinergic.
source: Of these LHON cell types, 26 were acetylcholinergic (Figure 2), 13 GABAergic (Figure 3) and nine were glutamatergic (Figure 3)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Of the identified LHON cell types, 13 were GABAergic.
source: Of these LHON cell types, 26 were acetylcholinergic (Figure 2), 13 GABAergic (Figure 3) and nine were glutamatergic (Figure 3)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Of the identified LHON cell types, nine were glutamatergic.
source: Of these LHON cell types, 26 were acetylcholinergic (Figure 2), 13 GABAergic (Figure 3) and nine were glutamatergic (Figure 3)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Three LHON cell types expressed multiple fast neurotransmitters.
source: Unexpectedly, we identified three cell types expressing multiple fast neurotransmitters (Figures 2 and 3, white asterisks).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Two cell types, AV2a1/a4 and AV2b1/b2, were identified as both cholinergic and GABAergic.
source: Two cell types, AV2a1/a4 and AV2b1/b2, were identified as both cholinergic and GABAergic, indicating dual excitatory and inhibitory action.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claim: AV7a1 expressed markers for both acetylcholine and glutamate.
source: Similarly, AV7a1 expressed markers for both acetylcholine and glutamate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No direct descending output from the LH to the ventral nerve cord was identified.
source: As the presumptive site of innate olfactory processing, we were surprised to identify no direct descending output to the ventral nerve cord, although this was consistent with previous studies (Hsu and Bhandawat, 2016; Namiki et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Only one cell type projecting to the central complex was found.
source: We found only one cell type projecting to the central complex, a sensory-motor integration center (Pfeiffer and Homberg, 2014; Wolff et al., 2015) (glutamatergic LHON PV5k1 projecting to layer 2 of the fan-shaped body)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text with citations to support the function of the central complex.

claim: No direct projections to the ellipsoid body were found.
source: and no direct projections to the ellipsoid body, which has been implicated in aversive chemotaxis (Gao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text with a citation to support the function of the ellipsoid body.

claim: Three bilateral LHONs connecting both hemispheres of the brain were identified.
source: We also identified three bilateral LHONs connecting both hemispheres of the brain and confirmed their projections using single-cell labelling (Nern et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text with a citation to the method used.

claim: Two of the bilateral LHONs were cholinergic: AD1e1 and AD3b1.
source: Two were cholinergic bilateral LHONs, AD1e1 a fruitless-positive cell type also known as aSP-g (Cachero et al., 2010; Kohl et al., 2013) and AD3b1, while the other was PV5k1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PV5k1 is a bilateral LHON.
source: Two were cholinergic bilateral LHONs, AD1e1 a fruitless-positive cell type also known as aSP-g (Cachero et al., 2010; Kohl et al., 2013) and AD3b1, while the other was PV5k1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: LHLNs were either GABAergic or glutamatergic.
source: LHLNs were either GABAergic or glutamatergic (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: The majority of local neuron cell types were constituents of four different primary neurite tracts, with all cell types in a tract positive for the same neurotransmitter.
source: Indeed we found the majority of local neuron cell types were constituents of four different primary neurite tracts, with all cell types in a tract positive for the same neurotransmitter (glutamatergic PV4 and PD3, GABAergic AV4 and PV2) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: LHINs were either cholinergic, GABAergic or both.
source: We identified 'good' or 'ideal' lines for 14 LHINs and characterized their principal fast neurotransmitter (Figure 5), finding that LHINs were either cholinergic, GABAergic or both.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Novel LHINs include projections from the wedge and inferior posterior slope in the auditory and mechanosensory system.
source: These Novel LHINs include projections from the wedge and inferior posterior slope in the auditory and mechanosensory system (Figure 5, WED-PN1-6) (Clemens et al., 2015; Matsuo et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5 and citations.

claim: Novel LHINs include projections from the lobula in the visual system.
source: the lobula in the visual system (Figure 5, LO-PN1-2)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Novel LHINs include projections from the gustatory subesophageal zone.
source: and the gustatory subesophageal zone (Figure 5, GNG-PN1).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: A putative ascending neuron with dendrites in the gustatory system was identified.
source: We also identified a putative ascending neuron with dendrites in the gustatory system (Figure 5, VNC-PN1 and Figure 4-figure supplement 1D'-D'').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5 and Figure 4-figure supplement 1D'-D''.

claim: The majority of LH output converged to the superior lateral protocerebrum (SLP).
source: Although LHONs had axons in 24 different neuropils, we found the majority of LH output converged to the superior lateral protocerebrum (SLP), where arborization was broad (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), followed by two other nearby neuropils, the superior intermediate protocerebrum (SIP) and the superior medial protocerebrum (SMP) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The SLP, SIP, and SMP are the next, third-order olfactory processing nodes.
source: This indicates that these regions, in particular the SLP are the next, third-order olfactory processing nodes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the overlap analysis data showing convergence of LHON axons in these regions.

claim: Two clear clusters of LHONs with axons co-projecting to the same location in the SLP were found.
source: We found two clear clusters of LHONs with axons co-projecting ot the same location, both in the SLP (Figure 6B, orange and blue borders).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: One cluster of LHONs received mostly excitatory LHONs.
source: One of these received mostly excitatory LHONs (Figure 6B, blue)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: One cluster of LHONs received a mix of cholinergic, GABAergic and glutamatergic LHONs.
source: while the other cluster received a mix of cholinergic, GABAergic and glutamatergic LHONs (Figure 6B, orange)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: There is not a strong relationship between LHON axonal and dendritic overlap (R2 = 0.094).
source: We did not find a strong relationship between LHON axonal and dendritic overlap (R2 = 0.094, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: LHLNs could be sorted into two broad groupings based on the degree of overlap with LHON dendrites in the lateral horn.
source: We found that LHLNs could be sorted into two broad groupings based on the degree of overlap (most or many) with LHON dendrites in the lateral horn (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6D.

claim: PN axons coarsely segregated LHON dendrites into three clusters.
source: We found a broad range of overlap (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A). PN axons coarsely segregated LHON dendrites into three clusters, two groups of LHONs that potentially receive input from many PNs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A', e.g. AV1a1, AV6b1) and one group of LHONs that overlap with the PNs of only a few glomeruli (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A', e.g. PV5k1, AV2b1/b2).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The DA2, DL4 and VA7l glomeruli all specifically encode aversive olfactory odours.
source: We examined glomeruli that have clear functions in olfactory behaviour such as avoidance and approach to ecologically critical odours. The DA2, DL4 and VA7l glomeruli all specifically encode aversive olfactory odours (Ebrahim et al., 2015; Mansourian et al., 2016; Stensmyr et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: The VM1 glomerulus encodes attractive amines.
source: Surprisingly, the VM1 glomerulus, which encodes attractive amines (Min et al., 2013) also had a high overlap score for these LHONs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A', green box).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it, and the overlap finding is supported by data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A'.

claim: PNs from the V glomerulus mediate responses to CO2.
source: PNs with dendrites in the V glomerulus mediate responses to CO2 (Lin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: PNs from the V glomerulus have diverse anatomies and project to the LH in parallel to mediate CO2 aversion in a concentration dependent manner.
source: Unlike most glomeruli (Jefferis et al., 2007; Kazama and Wilson, 2009), PNs from the V glomerulus have diverse anatomies and project to the LH in parallel to mediate CO2 aversion in a concentration dependent manner (Lin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: Multimodal input to the LH is restricted to a limited ventral zone.
source: This analysis clearly demonstrates that multimodal input to the LH is restricted to a limited ventral zone (Figure 7D–E), with the most extensive inputs coming from the mechanosensory and auditory system (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 7D-E.

claim: The LH consists of a multimodal ventral zone and an olfactory privileged dorsal segment.
source: Thus, the LH consists of a multimodal ventral zone and an olfactory privileged dorsal segment with LHONs potentially capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities.
evidence: This is an inference based on the multimodal input data showing restricted ventral input.

claim: Many, but not all LHONs converged with DAN dendrites.
source: We created masks for DAN dendrites and systematically compared their overlap with LHON axons (Figure 8A, see Figure 8C' for example overlay), finding that many, but not all LHONs converged with DAN dendrites.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 8A.

claim: LHONs were proximal to the dendrites of DANs from both the PAM and PPL1 clusters.
source: LHONs were proximal to the dendrites of DANs from both the PAM and PPL1 clusters (Mao and Davis, 2009), activity in which are necessary to induce appetitive and aversive memories respectively (Aso and Rubin, 2016; Claridge-Chang et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text with citations to support the function of DANs.

claim: Several instances of overlap between MBON and LHON axons were identified.
source: To identify downstream sites of convergence between the LH and MB outputs, we performed the above analysis with MBONs, identifying several instances of overlap between MBON and LHON axons (Figure 8B, see Figure 8C'–C''' for overlaid examples).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 8B.

claim: 70% of LHON axons did not have a significant overlap with any DAN dendrite or MBON axon.
source: We found that 70% of LHON axons did not have a significant overlap with any DAN dendrite or MBON axon; only 16% of identified LHONs had a significant overlap with a MBON.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text based on overlap analysis.

claim: Only 16% of identified LHONs had a significant overlap with a MBON.
source: We found that 70% of LHON axons did not have a significant overlap with any DAN dendrite or MBON axon; only 16% of identified LHONs had a significant overlap with a MBON.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text based on overlap analysis.

claim: AD1b2 neurons receive input from MBON-α1.
source: We first confirmed our light-level pre that AD1b2 neurons receive input from MBON-α1 (Figure 8D' and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by EM data in Figure 8D'.

claim: MBON-γ5β′2a, MBON-α′2, and MBON-γ2α′1 form synapses onto the axonal segment of AD1b2 neurons.
source: For all three of these MBONs we observed synapses from the MBON onto the axonal segment of the LHON, indicating that the AD1b2 axonal compartment integrates MB output (Figure 8D–8E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by EM data in Figure 8D-8E.

claim: MBON input to AD1b2 was variable across individual AD1b2 cells.
source: This input was variable across individual AD1b2 cells (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 8E.

claim: MBON-γ2α′1 and MBON-γ5β′2 drive both sleep and valence behaviour in opposite directions.
source: MBON-γ2α′1 and MBON-γ5β′2 drive both sleep and valence behaviour in opposite directions, while expressing different neurotransmitters (MBON-γ2α'1 is cholinergic while MBON-γ5β′2 is glutamatergic) (Aso et al., 2014b; Sitaraman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: AD1b2 LHONs integrate information in three separate domains: From AL PNs on their dendrites within the LH, from MBON-α1 on dendrites outside the LH and from MBON-γ5β′2, MBON-α′two and MBON-γ2α′one on their axon terminals.
source: AD1b2 LHONs integrate information in three separate domains: From AL PNs on their dendrites within the LH, from MBON-α1 on dendrites outside the LH and from MBON-γ5β′2, MBON-α′two and MBON-γ2α′one on their axon terminals.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings about AD1b2 connectivity based on EM data.

claim: A subset of ~30% of LHONs interact with the MB neurons.
source: In summary, a subset of ~30% of LHONs interact with the MB neurons: they can potentially modulate DANs, co-converge onto common downstream targets with MBONs and axoaxonically integrate MB information during olfactory processing.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings about LHON-MB interactions based on overlap and EM data.

claim: 89 split-GAL4 lines were screened in the optogenetic valence assay.
source: We performed a screen on a subset of LH neurons using mostly 'ideal' split-GAL4 lines and, where possible, multiple lines per cell type (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A). We screened 89 split-GAL4 lines (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A), covering 50 cell types (and some combinatorial split-GAL4 lines, see Supplementary file 3)
evidence: This is a primary methodological detail stated in the text and shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 15 split-GAL4 lines that drove valence behaviour (approach or aversion) were identified.
source: and identified 15 lines that drove valence behaviour (approach or aversion; Figure 9B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9B.

claim: Three split-GAL4 lines induced approach when stimulated.
source: Three lines (each labelling different cell types) induced approach (e.g. Figure 9C')
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9C'.

claim: 12 split-GAL4 lines drove aversion when stimulated.
source: and 12 drove aversion (e.g. Figure 9C'') when stimulated.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9C''.

claim: Aversive split-GAL4 lines together labeled six different cell types.
source: Aversive split-GAL4 lines together labeled six different cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claim: Four aversive cell types (AV1a1, PV4a1:5, PV5a1, PV5c1) were covered by more than one split-GAL4 line.
source: Four of these (AV1a1, PV4a1:5, PV5a1, PV5c1) were covered by more than one split-GAL4 line (Figure 9B), driving a valence phenotype (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9B.

claim: All lines containing AV1a1 or PV4a1:5 showed significant aversion.
source: We focused on the first two cell types for further analysis because all lines containing those cell types showed significant aversion.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claim: Consistent aversion compared to the control was observed for lines labelling AV1a1 and PV4a1:5 in a second assay.
source: In this second assay, we observed consistent aversion compared to the control for lines labelling AV1a1 and PV4a1:5 (Figure 9D), confirming that these cell types drive avoidance behaviour
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9D.

claim: PV4a1/a2 neurons are synaptically connected to AV1a1 neurons.
source: To determine this, we examined synapses onto AV1a1 neurons (AV1a1#1–2, which have been identified and reconstructed in Huoviala et al., 2018), confirming that PV4a1:5 and AV1a1 are synaptically connected (Figure 9F'').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by EM data in Figure 9F''.

claim: Together, PV4a1:2 account for 2.5% of postsynapses onto the AV1a1 dendrite.
source: Together, PV4a1:2 account for 2.5% of postsynapses onto the AV1a1 dendrite.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text based on EM data.

claim: Three split-GAL4 lines drive approach when their neurons were optogenetically stimulated.
source: Finally, we identified three split-GAL4 lines that drive approach when their neurons were optogenetically stimulated.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text.

claim: Only one of the three approach-driving split-GAL4 lines, LH1538, was truly cell type specific.
source: However, only one of these, LH1538 was truly cell type specific (Figure 9—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9—figure supplement 1E.

claim: LH1538 labeled AD1b2.
source: This line labeled AD1b2, which we previously identified as integrating input from MBONs (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 8F.

claim: Two additional lines that specifically label AD1b2 drove attraction.
source: To confirm that stimulation of AD1b2 can induce approach behaviour we tested two additional lines that specifically label this cell type in our valence assay, both of which drove attraction (Figure 9G, see Figure 9—figure supplement 1G for expression patterns).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9G.

claim: Only a small proportion (~15%) of split-GAL4 lines tested drove valence behaviour.
source: However, only a small proportion (~15%) of split-GAL4 lines tested (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A) drove such valence behaviour (Figure 9H).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A and Figure 9H.

claim: AV6a1 drives an initial increase in forward locomotion when stimulated.
source: We successfully replicated a locomotion phenotype with only one cell type, AV6a1, which drives an initial increase in forward locomotion when stimulated (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 10B.

claim: For two split-GAL4 lines labelling AV6a1, an increase in locomotion relative to the empty split-GAL4 control was found.
source: For two split-GAL4 lines labelling AV6a1 (Figure 10C, see Figure 8—figure supplement 1D for full expression patterns), we found an increase in locomotion relative to the empty split-GAL4 control (Figure 10D)
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 10C and 10D.

claim: Driving activity in AD3b1 neurons resulted in increased yaw turning by modulation of the left and right wingbeat amplitudes.
source: For all three cell types, we found differential effects of optogenetic stimulation on motor parameters relative to the controls not expressing an optogenetic effector (Figure 10I–K). Driving activity in AD3b1 neurons resulted in increased yaw turning by modulation of the left and right wingbeat amplitudes (Figure 10I).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 10I.
